subject: Adding covariates to a bivariate latent change score model using 'add = ' function

messages.author: cbbace2d981882b0
messages.subject: Adding covariates to a bivariate latent change score model using 'add = ' function
parts:
Hi Everyone,                                                                                                                                        I am using the lcsm package which creates lavaan code to run a bivariate latent change score model. I would like to add covariates to the model using the 'add = ' function, to regress age, sex and ancestry variables at baseline on both constructs (x and y) at each timepoint, and on both constructs' latent change scores. Below is the code for this, but running this did not work as nothing happens when I run it in R. Am I doing something wrong? Any help would be much appreciated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           model1 <- fit_bi_lcsm(data = dataset_1,

                       var_x = c("x_t1”, " x_t2", " x_t3"),

                       var_y = c("y_t1", " y_t2", " y_t3"),

                       model_x = list(alpha_constant = FALSE,

                                      beta = TRUE, phi = TRUE),

                       model_y = list(alpha_constant = TRUE,

                                      beta = FALSE, phi = TRUE),

                       coupling = list(xi_lag_yx = TRUE,

                                       delta_con_yx=TRUE,

                                       delta_con_xy=TRUE),

                       add = "x1 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "x2 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "x3 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "y1 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "y2 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "y3 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "dx2 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "dx3 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "dy2 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment",

                       "dy3 ~ ancestry_binary + sex_fromID + age_atenrolment")                                                                                                                                                                                                Kind regards,
Marcel
